newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends down, hits six-year low.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends down, hits six-year low.

text.p: The won fell against the dollar on Monday, hitting a six-year low of 832.80 in the afternoon, dealers said.
It is the lowest level for the won since South Korea introduced a market average system in March 1990.
The won ended at 831.80 after opening at 829.70. It hit a high of 829.50.
Dealers said heavy import deals and the dollar's strength against the Japanese yen in the world markets sparked active dollar buying.
Fear of a central bank intervention kept banks from dumping the local currency in the morning, they said. But when the intervention failed to materialise, banks rushed to buy the U.S. unit.
"The resistance of 830 was broken due to severe shortage of dollars in the market," said one dealer.
Traders said the won was expected to trade in a range of 830 to 833.50 on Tuesday. The base mid-rate is seen at 831.00 compared with today's 829.00.
